generation.final_prompt:
Rendering style:
Create an authored editorial illustration for a serious technology newspaper.

Direction:
- authored editorial print language
- deliberate simplified shapes with clear focal hierarchy
- restrained limited palette
- subtle physical print texture
- controlled abstraction and strong negative space
- non-photorealistic but factually grounded representation
- newspaper and social-card readability

Fixed factual and safety restrictions:
- Do not render visible text, captions, headlines, or newspaper typography.
- Do not render logos or trademarks.
- Do not fabricate visible factual evidence.
- Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
- Do not imitate a named or living artist.

Profile-specific exclusions:
- glossy CGI
- luxury product render
- generic futuristic concept art
- cyberpunk or neon
- glowing circuit-board decoration
- floating particles
- heroic centered hardware
- server rack treated as monument or skyscraper
- generic server room
- advertising composition
- airbrushed gradients
- synthetic chrome
- excessive pseudo-technical detail
- malformed or visible text
- labels
- diagrams with words

Exact source facts:
Title: MICROSOFT RESEARCHERS SHOW AI AGENTS CAN BE BACKDOORED BY EDITING FEWER THAN 10 NEURONS
Summary: Microsoft researchers demonstrated “Lazarus,” a method that edits fewer than 10 rarely used neurons in an open-weight model to embed a hidden command. When a trigger appears in a prompt or tool output, an agent may execute attacker-controlled commands with its existing permissions. Testing achieved 98.8% on Nemotron-Terminal-8B using seven edited neurons. Microsoft advises comparing checkpoints with base weights, using private model registries, sandboxing agent code, limiting network access, and requiring approval for high-impact actions.

Editorial idea:
A barely altered AI model can conceal a command that activates only when the right trigger appears, turning ordinary agent permissions into an attack path.

Central subject:
A compromised AI agent model with a hidden trigger embedded in its neural network

Visual relationship:
The tiny model alteration is visually set against the potentially large consequences of commands executed with the agent's existing permissions.

Composition:
Show a clean sequence of ordinary agent instructions passing through a nearly imperceptible concealed alteration, with one triggered instruction emerging as a clearly dangerous action at the far end. Keep the intervention small and the resulting consequence visually disproportionate.

Permitted literal elements:
An abstract neural network with a very small highlighted cluster of altered nodes
A stream of ordinary prompt and tool-output forms entering the model
One distinct trigger signal passing through the altered region
A separated execution area showing an unauthorized command being activated
A visible boundary representing the agent's existing permissions

Abstraction level:
medium

Story-specific forbidden elements:
Racks
Chips
Laptops
Robots
Clouds
Shields
Arrows
Charts
Skyscrapers
Chess
Handshakes
Split-screen conflict
Artist imitation
Rendered text
Logos
Unsupported physical details

Likely failure modes to avoid:
Making the altered neurons appear large or obvious rather than fewer than 10
Suggesting the model independently gains new privileges instead of abusing existing permissions
Depicting a generic cybersecurity breach without the hidden-trigger mechanism
Using decorative AI imagery disconnected from the demonstrated backdoor

Global factual restrictions:
Do not fabricate visible factual evidence. Do not imitate a named or living artist. Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
Do not render any words, letters, numbers, labels, captions, annotations, signage, diagrams with text, logos, watermarks, or pseudo-writing anywhere in the image.
If the concept cannot be represented without visible text, represent the relationship through shape, scale, spacing, direction, grouping, interruption, containment, or contrast instead.
